name: L-tyrosine
short: In a 4-week crossover trial in 30 healthy men, adverse events were comparable to placebo and none were serious. High doses in a 13-week rat study affected the liver and kidneys.
text: In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in 30 healthy adult men given graded doses of L-tyrosine up to 4 g per day for 4 weeks each, no serious adverse events occurred, mild-to-moderate adverse events were about as frequent as with placebo, and no dose-related abnormalities appeared in blood tests; the study covered only healthy men and 4-week periods. In animal data, a 13-week study in rats found swelling (oedema) of the surface layer of the forestomach in females at 600 mg per kg of body weight per day and in both sexes at 2000 mg/kg per day, and liver changes (increased weight with slight rises in liver enzymes) and kidney changes at 2000 mg/kg per day; the authors put the no-observed-adverse-effect level at 600 mg/kg per day in males and 200 mg/kg per day in females. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
